# Daniel 6 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** It pleased Darius to set over the kingdom 120 satraps, to be throughout the whole kingdom,

**2** Daniel continued to describe the lions' den as revealed by God.

**10** And Daniel, when-he-knew that the-document was-signed, went to-his-house — and-windows [were]-opened for-him in-his-upper-chamber toward Jerusalem — and-three times in the day he-was-kneeling upon his-knees and-praying and-giving-thanks before his-God, just-as he-had-been-doing before.

**16** Then the-king commanded, and-they-brought Daniel and-cast-him into the den-of the-lions. The-king answered and-said to-Daniel, "Your-God whom you serve continually — He will-deliver-you!"

**17** Daniel continued to describe the lions' den as revealed by God.

**18** Daniel continued to describe the lions' den as revealed by God.

**19** Daniel continued to describe the lions' den as revealed by God.

**20** Daniel continued to describe the lions' den as revealed by God.

**22** "My-God sent His-angel and-shut the-lions' mouths, and-they-did-not-hurt-me, because before-Him innocence was-found in-me; and-also before-you, O-king, I-have-done no wrong."

**23** Daniel continued to describe the lions' den as revealed by God.

**24** Daniel continued to describe the lions' den as revealed by God.

**25** Daniel continued to describe the lions' den as revealed by God.

**26** "I-make a-decree, that in-all the-dominion-of my-kingdom men tremble and-fear before the-God-of Daniel; for He [is] the-living God, and-enduring forever, and-His-kingdom [is one] which will-not-be-destroyed, and-His-dominion [shall be] until the-end."

**27** Daniel continued to describe the lions' den as revealed by God.

**28** Daniel continued to describe the lions' den as revealed by God.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

- **6:1**: The the lions' den passage opens within its historical and literary context in the book of Daniel.

- **6:14**: The sealed den imagery serves Daniel's larger theological argument about divine sovereignty over history.

- **6:28**: The chapter closes affirming God's control over the rise and fall of empires.

— LOGOS
